prompt: In which quadrant is the point $(3, -5)$?
hint: The signs of the coordinates decide the quadrant. Look at whether each coordinate of this point is positive or negative.

hints.text: The signs of the coordinates decide the quadrant. Look at whether each coordinate of this point is positive or negative.
Here $x = 3$ is positive, so the point is right of the $y$-axis, and $y = -5$ is negative, so it is below the $x$-axis. Recall the quadrants are numbered counter-clockwise from the upper right.
Right and below is the lower-right region, which is Quadrant IV, so the answer is $4$.

explanation: The $x$-coordinate is $3$, which is positive, so the point lies to the right of the $y$-axis.
The $y$-coordinate is $-5$, which is negative, so the point lies below the $x$-axis.
Quadrants are numbered I to IV counter-clockwise starting from the upper right, so the lower-right region is the fourth.
The point $(3, -5)$ is in Quadrant IV, so the answer is $4$.
